About

Reece has taught me that kids don’t all learn the same way - and honestly, that’s what makes them so interesting.

He learns best with bright colors, time outside, a little imagination, and something fun enough to actually keep his mind engaged. Watching what works for him made me realize how important it is to meet kids where they are instead of expecting every child to learn the exact same way.

Some kids need movement. Some need color. Some need a story, a challenge, a favorite animal, or something completely ridiculous enough to make them curious.

So if there’s something your child loves, something that helps them focus, or something you’d like to see included, please tell me. I want these games to feel like they were made with real kids in mind - because they were.

This started with one kid, one very random idea, and a lot of poisoned hot dogs.

Made for kids, inspired by kids, and hopefully shaped by them too.

This whole thing started with my four-year-old nephew, Reece, who somehow gets bigger and smarter every time I see him.

One day, he made his mom call me because he had a very important request: he wanted me to make a game called “Stay Away From Poison Hotdogs.”

No explanation. No backstory. Just a four-year-old with a title, a vision, and complete confidence that I would make it happen.

Reece also loves dinosaurs, so naturally they had to become part of the chaos too. Somehow, one very random phone call turned into this silly, colorful, slightly ridiculous little game.

So really, this all started with Reece, dinosaurs, and one very important rule:

Stay away from poison hotdogs.

To this day, I still have absolutely no idea why the hotdogs are poisoned.
